Rashi on Yevamot 25b:10:1.hebrew: לעולם בחד - ודקשיא לך, מדקתני שאסר, מכלל דבר מישרי הוא — אין, ביחיד מומחה, וכדרב חסדא בנדרי' בפרק נערה המאורסה:
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:10:1.english: Actually, [it is] with a single [judge] - And [as for] what was difficult for you — [namely, that] since it teaches "who forbade," [this implies] that he is one [qualified] to permit — yes, [it is] with a single expert, and [it is] in accordance with [the statement of] Rav Chisda in Nedarim, in the chapter Na'arah HaMe'orasah.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:12:1.hebrew: לא חשו חכמים לדבר זה - לומר לא יקחו שוב שדה זו מן הלוקח, וכן העד של גט לא ישא את האשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:12:1.english: The Sages were not concerned about this matter - To say [that] they may not subsequently purchase this field from the buyer, and likewise, the witness on [the] bill of divorce may not marry the woman.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:12:2.hebrew: היא גופה - כלומר, ה"ה דתרי נמי לא חשידי. והא דקתני שהוא ב"ד, לאו משום לאפוקי מחשדא, אלא לאשמועי' דאין מיאון בפחות מג', ולאפוקי ממאן דאמר בפ' [ב"ש] (לקמן יבמות קז:) מיאון בשנים:
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:12:2.english: This itself - That is to say, the same applies that two [judges] are also not suspected [of collaborating]. And that which [the Mishnah] teaches that it is a court is not in order to exclude suspicion, rather to teach us that there is no refusal [of marriage] before fewer than three [judges], and to exclude [the opinion of] the one who said in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai (below, Yevamot 107b) [that] refusal [may be performed] before two [judges].

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:13:1.english: [If] he married [her], what is [the law] as to whether he must divorce [her]? - [This] refers to the sage and to the one who brings a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:14:1.english: Tradition or reasoning - [Referring to] this that you said: "[If] he married [her], he does not remove [her]."

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:1:1.hebrew: גזלן דדבריהם - כמו מפריחי יונים ומשחק בקוביא, דתנן (ר"ה דף כב.): כל העדות שאין האשה כשרה לה, אף הן אינם כשרים. ועלה אמר רב מנשה: זאת אומרת, גזלן דדבריהם כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:1:1.english: A robber according to their [i.e., the Sages'] words - Such as pigeon-flyers and a dice-player, as we learned in a mishnah (Rosh Hashanah 22a): Any testimony for which a woman is not fit, they too are not fit. And concerning it Rav Menashe said: That is to say, a robber according to their words, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:2:1.hebrew: רבא פליג עליה דרב יוסף ואמר: <abbr title="אפילו">אפי'</abbr> אמר פלוני רבעני לרצוני, הוא ואחר מצטרף להורגו לרובע; דכיון שזה מתכוין לעדות, נאמן הוא אצל חברו, ואין נאמן על עצמו ממה שאמר לרצוני, דאדם קרוב אצל עצמו, וקרוב פסול לעדות בין לטובה בין לרעה. הלכך, אינו נעשה רשע בעדות עצמו:
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:2:1.english: Rava disagrees with Rav Yosef and says: Even if [a man] said, "So-and-so sodomized me with my consent," he and another [witness] combine to have the sodomizer executed; for since this [person] intends to give testimony, he is believed regarding his fellow, but he is not believed regarding himself as to what he said, "with my consent," because a person is a relative to himself, and a relative is disqualified from testifying, whether for [one's] benefit or to [one's] detriment. Therefore, he does not become wicked through his own testimony.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:2:2.hebrew: ואין אדם משים - את עדותו עדות אצל עצמו ליעשות רשע. והא דקי"ל (ב"מ דף ג:) הודאת פיו כמאה עדים דמי, הנ"מ לממונא, אבל לקנסא ולעונש מלקות וליפסל, לא:
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:2:2.english: And a person does not make - his testimony [valid] testimony regarding himself so as to be rendered wicked. And [as for] that which we hold as established (Bava Metzia 3b), [that] one's own admission is equivalent to a hundred witnesses — that applies only to monetary matters, but regarding a fine, the punishment of lashes, or being disqualified [from testifying], [it does] not.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:3:1.hebrew: ושאני עדות אשה דאקילו בה רבנן - הלכך, אפילו רשע נאמן, ואנא לית לי דרב מנשיא דאמר: הא דדברי תורה פסול:
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:3:1.english: And testimony [concerning] a woman is different, as the Rabbis were lenient regarding it - Therefore, even a wicked person is believed, and I do not accept [the opinion of] Rav Menasya, who said: One [who is wicked] by Torah law is disqualified.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:3:2.hebrew: אלא רב מנשיא דאמר כרבי יהודה - והכי מיתוקם סוגיא: רב יוסף מוקים לרב מנשיא כרבי יהודה, ורב מנשיא מוקי לרב יוסף כרבי יהודה:
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:3:2.english: Rather, Rav Menashya spoke in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - And thus the sugya is established: Rav Yosef establishes Rav Menashya [as holding] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, and Rav Menashya establishes Rav Yosef [as holding] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:4:1.english: I was with his murderers - but I did not touch him.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:6:1.hebrew: ע"י לסטיות - לפי שהיה עמהן:
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:6:1.english: On account of armed banditry - Because he was with them.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:7:1.hebrew: בנדר - שנדרה הנאה מבעלה, ולא הפר לה, ובאתה לחכם להתיר לה, ולא מצא פתח לחרטה:
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:7:1.english: By a vow - That she vowed [to derive no] benefit from her husband, and he did not nullify [it] for her, and she came to a Sage to dissolve [it] for her, and he did not find an opening for regret.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:7:2.english: He may not marry her - Because of suspicion.

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:7:3.hebrew: שהוא ב"ד - כלומר, מיאון או חליצה לא עשה חכם זה ביחידי, דקי"ל חליצה ומיאון בג', ותלתא לא חשידי:
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:7:3.english: That he is a court - That is to say, this Sage did not perform refusal or ḥalitza alone, for we hold that ḥalitza and refusal [are performed] before three [judges], and three are not suspected [of impropriety].

Rashi on Yevamot 25b:8:1.hebrew: הא התירה - ואח"כ מת בעלה או גירשה, ישאנה, שאין כאן חשדא:
Rashi on Yevamot 25b:8:1.english: This [implies that if] he rendered her permitted - and afterward her husband died or divorced her, he may marry her, for there is no suspicion here.

Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:11:1.hebrew: טעמא דב"ד, הא בי תרי לא - ואע"ג דאמרינן בריש השולח (גיטין דף לב: ושם) דלתרי נמי בי דינא קרו להו, מ"מ אור"י דדייק שפיר, דמדתלי טעמא בבית דין ולא קאמר "מפני שהיו ב'", ש"מ דלא סגי הכא בתרי. ועוד: דומיא דחליצה דבג'; אע"ג דאיכא מאן דמכשר בפרק מצות חליצה (לקמן יבמות דף קד.) ביחידי, הך תנא לא סבר לה כוותיה, דחד ודאי לא מיקרי ב"ד, ואיכא נמי רננה בחד:
Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:11:1.english: The reason is [that it was] a court; then, [with] two, [he may] not [marry her] - Even though we say at the beginning of [the chapter] HaSholeach (Gittin 32b and elsewhere [there]) that two [judges] are also called a court (bei dina), nevertheless, the Ri says that [the Gemara] infers well: since [the Mishnah] bases the reason on "a court" and does not say "because there were two," derive from this that two do not suffice here. Furthermore, [refusal must be] similar to chalitzah, which is [performed] before three [judges]; even though there is an opinion that validates [chalitzah] before a single [judge] in the chapter Mitzvat Chalitzah (later, Yevamot 104a), this Tanna does not hold like him, for a single [judge] is certainly not called a court, and there is also [concern for] gossip with a single [judge].

Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:12:1.hebrew: לא חשו חכמים לדבר זה - ואע"ג דשרי, מ"מ בעל נפש יתרחק, כדתני' עלה באלו טרפות (חולין דף מד: ושם): "דן את הדין, זיכה וחייב, טימא וטיהר, וכן העדים שהעידו — כולם רשאים ליקח, אבל חכמים אמרו: התרחק מן הכיעור ומן הדומה לו". וא"ת: הא אמרינן בסוף התקבל (גיטין דף סז. ושם) גבי "חיישינן שמא תשכור עדים": "דיבורא אמרי, מעשה לא עבדי"? וי"ל, דכשמעידים שקר חשיב נמי מעשה כדפי' בקונטרס, כיון דעל פיהם נגמר; ולא קרי דיבורא התם אלא באומר "אמרו", שאומר מן הבעל לסופר ולעדים לכתוב ולחתום, דלא נגמר הדבר על ידיהם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:12:1.english: The Sages were not concerned about this matter - Even though it is permitted, nevertheless a scrupulous person should distance himself [from it], as is taught [in a baraita] regarding this in [the chapter] Eilu Tereifot (Chullin 44b, and [see] there): "[One who] judged a case, acquitted or found liable, declared impure or declared pure, and likewise the witnesses who testified — all of them are permitted to purchase [it], but the Sages said: Distance yourself from ugliness and from anything similar to it." And if you will say: Do we not say at the end of [the chapter] Hamekabel (Gittin 67a, and [see] there), regarding [the statement] "we are concerned lest she hire witnesses": "They will speak [mere] words, [but] they will not perform an act"? And one can answer that when they testify falsely, it is also considered an act, as Rashi explained, since through their word [the matter] is finalized; and there [in Gittin], it is only called "[mere] words" in the case of one who says "Say [to them]" — that is, one who says on behalf of the husband to the scribe and to the witnesses to write and to sign [the bill of divorce] — for the matter is not finalized through them.

Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:14:1.hebrew: אמר להו מתני' היא הנטען כו' - ולנטען על אשת איש לא דמי, דהתם בדין שיוציא — אם הוא אמת אסירא ליה; אבל הכא שאסר את האשה בנדר, אפילו אסרה שלא כדין, כיון שגירשה בעלה — שריא לחכם מדאורייתא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:14:1.english: He said to them: It is the mishna, one suspected, etc. - And it is not comparable to one suspected [of adultery] with a married woman, for there it is fitting that he must divorce [her], [since] if it is true, she is forbidden to him. But here, where [the sage] forbade the woman through a vow, even if he forbade her improperly, once her husband divorced her, she is permitted to the sage by Torah law.

Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:2:1.hebrew: רבא אמר אדם קרוב אצל עצמו - הקשה ר' יצחק בן אברהם: דבפרק שני דכתובות (דף יח: ושם) מסיק רבא גופיה גבי הא דתנן התם: "אם אין כתב ידן יוצא ממקום אחר הרי אלו נאמנים לומר אנוסים היינו" — "לא שנו אלא שאמרו 'אנוסים היינו מחמת נפשות', אבל אמרו 'מחמת ממון' — אין נאמנים". ואמאי אין נאמנים? דהוה לן לפלוגי דיבורא ולומר דאנוסים היו, ולא מחמת ממון אלא מחמת נפשות! ואומר ר"י דלא פלגינן דיבורא כדי לפסול השטר, דמדאוריית' עדים החתומים על השטר נעשה כמי שנחקרה עדותן בב"ד. א"נ, התם בכל ענין שהם אנוסים, אם לא מחמת נפשות — הוו רשעים; הלכך לית לן למיתלי באונס מחמת נפשות, דהוי מיעוטא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:2:1.english: Rava said: A person is his own relative - Rabbi Yitzchak ben Avraham raised a difficulty: In the second chapter of Ketubot (18b and there), Rava himself concludes regarding that which we learned in the Mishnah there: "If their handwriting does not emerge from another place, they are believed to say, 'We were coerced'" — [Rava said:] "They taught [this] only where they said, 'We were coerced due to [danger to] lives,' but if they said, '[We were coerced] due to money,' they are not believed." And why are they not believed? For we ought to split the statement and say that they were coerced, and not due to money, rather due to [danger to] lives! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that we do not split a statement in order to invalidate a document, because by Torah law, witnesses signed on a document are treated as if their testimony has [already] been examined in court. Alternatively, there, in any case where they were coerced, if [it was] not due to [danger to] lives, they are wicked; therefore, we should not attribute [it] to coercion due to [danger to] lives, since that is a minority [of cases]:

Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:2:2.hebrew: ואין אדם משים עצמו רשע - היינו לפסול את עצמו, אבל נאמן הוא לומר גבי אכילת חלב "מזיד הייתי", כדאמר בכריתות (דף יב. ושם), דאין לנו לכופו להביא חולין לעזרה לפי דבריו. והא דקאמרינן בהאיש מקדש (קדושין דף נ. ושם) גבי "הבא לי מן החלון או מן הדלוסקמא", דלא עביד איניש דמשוי נפשיה רשיעא לומר "מזיד הייתי" — לאו משום שלא יהא נאמן לומר "מזיד הייתי", דפשיטא דנאמן, אלא כלומר שאין ברצון אומר בענין דמשוי נפשיה רשיעא. וא"ת: דהשתא משמע דנרבע לרצונו פסול לעדות, ובפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כו:) איכא למ"ד דחשוד על העריות כשר לעדות? וי"ל: דהתם בחשוד שהוא פריץ ומתייחד עם העריות, ולא ודאי בא על הערוה, כדפי' התם בקונטרס; ומאן דפריך התם: "עני מרי, ארבעים בכתפיה וכשר?!" — היינו משום דמלקין על "לא טובה השמועה". וא"ת: וכי ודאי בא על הערוה אמאי פסול? הא "רשע דחמס" בעינן, שיהא רע לשמים ולבריות, וזה אין רע לבריות — כגון אוכל נבלות להכעיס, דכשר לרבא בפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין כ"ז.)! וי"ל: דהוי כמו אוכל נבלות לתאבון, דפסול לכולי עלמא אע"פ שאין רע לבריות, דכיון דחשוד לעבור בשביל הנאת עצמו, חשוד נמי להעיד שקר בשביל ממון; והכי נמי בא על הערוה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:2:2.english: And a person does not make himself wicked - That is, [he is not believed] to disqualify himself [from testifying]; however, he is believed to say regarding eating forbidden fat (chelev), "I acted intentionally," as it says in Keritot (12a and there [in the parallel discussion]), since we cannot compel him to bring unconsecrated animals (chullin) into the Temple courtyard based on his own words. And as for that which we say in [the chapter] HaIsh Mekadesh (Kiddushin 50a and there) regarding "Bring me from the window or from the chest (deluskama)," that a person does not make himself wicked by saying "I acted intentionally" — it is not because he would not be believed to say "I acted intentionally," for it is obvious that he is believed; rather, it means that [a person] does not willingly speak in a manner that makes himself wicked. And if you ask: Now it is implied that one who is sodomized willingly is disqualified from testimony, whereas in the chapter Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 26b) there is an opinion that one who is suspected of forbidden sexual relations is fit for testimony? And it can be answered: There [it is speaking] of one who is suspected [merely] because he is licentious and secludes himself with forbidden women, and not [one who] definitely engaged in forbidden relations, as Rashi explained there. And the one who objects there, "Answer me, Master: forty [lashes] on his shoulders, yet he is fit?!" — that is because they administer lashes for "an evil report." And if you ask: Even when he definitely engaged in forbidden relations, why is he disqualified? Surely we require "a wicked person of violence," meaning one who is bad to Heaven and to people, whereas this one is not bad to people — like one who eats non-kosher meat (nevelot) out of spite, who is fit [to testify] according to Rava in the chapter Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 27a)! And it can be answered: It is like one who eats nevelot out of appetite, who is disqualified according to everyone even though he is not bad to people, because since he is suspected of transgressing for his own pleasure, he is also suspected of testifying falsely for money — and so too [with] one who engages in forbidden relations.

Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:3:1.hebrew: לימא רב יוסף דאמר כרבי יהודה - תימה, דהכא לרבי יהודה לית ליה פלגינן דיבורא; ובפרק החולץ (לקמן יבמות דף מז. ושם) אמרינן: ההוא דאתא לקמיה דרבי יהודה ואמר "נתגיירתי ביני לבין עצמי", א"ל: "נאמן אתה לפסול את עצמך, ואי אתה יכול לפסול את בניך", אלמא פלגינן דיבורא! ומיהו י"ל, דהתם לא מטעם עדות נאמן (דהא אדם קרוב אצל עצמו, ועוד, דאם נאמן לפסול עצמו איך יתכן שיהו בניו כשרים?), אלא הא דפסלינן היינו לאוסרו בבת ישראל, דשויה אנפשיה חתיכה דאיסורא, או אם נגח שור של ישראל את שורו פטור, מטעם הודאת בעל דין. וההיא דר' יהודה גופא קשיא, ושם נפרש בעזרת השם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:3:1.english: "Shall we say that Rav Yosef spoke in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda?" - It is puzzling: here, according to Rabbi Yehuda, he does not hold of [the principle of] palginan dibbura [splitting a statement]; yet in Chapter HaCholetz (later, Yevamot 47a and there [in the commentary]), [the Gemara] states: A certain man came before Rabbi Yehuda and said, "I converted privately on my own." [Rabbi Yehuda] said to him: "You are believed to disqualify yourself, but you cannot disqualify your children." Thus, we see that we do split a statement! However, one can answer that there he is not believed on the basis of testimony (for a person is a relative to himself [and therefore cannot testify about himself]; and furthermore, if he were believed [as a witness] to disqualify himself, how could it be that his children are fit?), rather, the reason we disqualify [him] is to forbid him from [marrying] a Jewish woman, because he has rendered himself a forbidden entity [chatikhah de'issura], or [that] if the ox of a Jew gored his ox, [the owner] is exempt, on the basis of a litigant's admission [hoda'at ba'al din]. And that [statement] of Rabbi Yehuda itself is difficult, and we will explain [it] there, with the help of God.

Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:4:1.hebrew: באומר אני הייתי עם הורגיו - אור"י דאע"ג דאמר "הרגנוהו", נעשה כאומר "אני הייתי עם הורגיו". וכענין זה מפרש ר"ת ורבינו חננאל בפ' מי שאחזו (גיטין עג: ד"ה אמר), "באומר מעת שאני בעולם" — נעשה כאומר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:4:1.english: Where he said: "I was with his murderers" - Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that even though he said, "We killed him," it is treated as if he said, "I was with his murderers." And in this manner Rabbeinu Tam and Rabbeinu Chananel explain in the chapter [entitled] Mi She'achazo (Gittin 73b, s.v. amar), "where he says: From the time I am in the world" — [that] it is treated as if he said [so].

Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:5:1.hebrew: במגיזת קפוטקיא - יש ספרים דגרסי במזיגת, והוי כמו במגיזת — עבראי, כמו שמלה שלמה. ר"י:
Tosafot on Yevamot 25b:5:1.english: In the passage [b'megizat] of Cappadocia - There are editions that read b'mezigat, and it is like b'megizat — [a transposition of letters], like simlah [and] salmah. [So explained] Rabbi Yitzchak:
